To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
interactive multimodal learning systems that are designed to be guided, interactive, and multimodal can be effective learning environments.

the design principles of guided activity, reflection on activity, feedback, control over the learning activity, and pretraining can be used to design multimodal interactive environments that are effective for learning.

guided activity, reflection on one’s learning, feedback on one’s performance, control of one’s learning process, and pretraining in the use of the learning environment promote students’ learning in a multimedia learning environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing interactive multimodal learning environment to promote students’ motivation and learning.
designing and evaluating multimodal learning environments that support the learning process.
the design of interactive multimodal learning environment to support students’ learning of complex concepts and skills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research in interactive multimodal learning is still in its infancy, and that there are many open questions to be answered in future studies.
the use of interactive multimodal learning environment can be beneficial for students in terms of learning and motivation.
interactive learning environments are a very powerful and useful tool for teaching and learning in all educational levels and in all subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design principles we have derived from our theoretical framework have been found to be effective in promoting learning in a variety of interactive multimodal learning environment.
the theory and the research have been successful in providing a framework for understanding how interactive multimedia learning environments can promote learning.

the design of interactive multimodal learning systems should be guided by the cognitive–affective processes of learning with media and that the design should include guided activity, reflection on learning, feedback, control over learning, and pretraining to promote learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning with technology is not a simple matter.

interactive multimodal learning systems can be designed to promote student learning, and that such design should be guided by the principles of guided activity, reflection and feedback, control, pretraining, and affect.
the use of interactive multimodal learning technologies should be guided by a theory of learning and that the design of these technologies should be informed by research on learning.
